Definition: from G1 (as a connective particle) and δελφύς (the womb); a brother (literally or figuratively) near or remote (much like G1):--brother.
BiblicalUsage: Adelphos is 'brother,' and the New Testament uses it constantly — for literal brothers like Andrew bringing Simon to Jesus, for fellow Jews, and above all for fellow believers. Jesus says whoever does the will of His Father is His brother, and John says love for the brethren is the mark of having passed from death to life. The word carries the whole weight of belonging to one family under one Father.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that adelphos is one of the great words of the New Testament because it refuses to let faith stay private. If God is our Father, then other believers are truly our brothers, and love for them is not optional — it is the evidence of life in us.
